why: Elbow flexed 90 degrees, side view along the hinge. Outer: the triceps line straight down to the joint (the triceps tendon is flat and thin over the distal humerus, so the back line above the point is a straight extension of the 30-60 mm line, as tools/anim/elbow_sweep.py olecranon() measures it), then the olecranon a defined point 5 mm proud of that line (the 4-6 mm target), 20 mm past the joint, then the forearm's back (the ulna's subcutaneous border) straight away from it. Inner: the biceps keeps its oval (shortened muscle bulges a little, o 1.04 at mid humerus), a crisp inner crease where the biceps and the forearm flexor lines meet (the cubital fossa folds, it does not web), the flexor mass 3 percent compressed next to it. Sources: surface anatomy of the flexed elbow (olecranon, epicondyles and the triceps tendon subcutaneous; the antecubital crease), the team's olecranon metric (elbow_sweep.py).
grammar: Control points in the strip's side view (tools/body/bends.py build_ref): seg p|d, s = fraction of that segment's rest length from the joint, side in|out, o = multiple of the body's OWN rest half-width there (measured on its rest strip), mm = added millimetres; line = the half-width extrapolated straight from two stations; arc = the outer corner swept from the proximal to the distal outer normal (fraction), corner = the two offset lines' meeting point (mm_bisect pushes it into the open sector: a web), tip = a bony point carried with the distal bone, sharp = a corner the smoothing keeps. Away from the joint o=1: the limb keeps its rest shape (a rigid bend); only the joint's own anatomy is authored.
